/assets/img/bioinformatics-walkthrough/a: Panel A shows the structures of five families of bacterial quorum-sensing signals. Panel B shows the agr locus of Paenibacillus, with the genes agrB, agrD, agrC, agrA and agrE drawn as arrows, and how the AgrD precursor peptide is processed into an autoinducing peptide that regulates antibiotic production
/assets/img/bioinformatics-walkthrough/b: Line plot of the BLASTP hits of PadeK against the clustered nr database: 5,000 accessions ranked by pE, with a dashed line at pE 60. The top hit has E = 0 and sits in a band above pE 180, the reporting limit of NCBI BLAST. The curve then declines gently from about 100 to about 75 over the first 700 accessions, drops to about 40 by accession 1,000, and flattens into a long tail that ends near 14; 820 hits are at or above pE 60
/assets/img/bioinformatics-walkthrough/g: Panel A shows five genes on a line of DNA, bracketed as one gene cluster. The first three follow one promoter and give one mRNA, and the last two follow a second promoter and give another mRNA. Panel B compares two donor genomes. Where the genes X, Y and Z are adjacent, one transferred DNA segment carries all three into the recipient genome. Where they are far apart, a segment of the same length carries only Y
/assets/img/bioinformatics-walkthrough/l: Structures of three lasso peptides, the gene clusters that encode them, and a scheme in which the B and C enzymes cleave off the leader peptide and close the ring
/assets/img/bioinformatics-walkthrough/p: Lasso peptide gene clusters containing a kinase gene in four bacterial strains, an alignment of their precursor peptides, the map of the expression plasmid, and chromatograms showing the lasso peptide and its phosphorylated form

A polycistronic operon. A stretch of DNA with two open reading frames is transcribed into one mRNA that has two protein-coding regions, each with its own ribosome-binding site, and the mRNA is translated into two proteins

Two panels. Panel A is a line plot of four PSI-BLAST cycles of PadeK against the clustered nr database, each with 5,000 accessions ranked by pE, and a dashed line at the inclusion threshold, pE 60. Hits with E = 0 sit in a band above pE 180, the reporting limit of NCBI BLAST: 1 in cycle 0, 254 in cycle 1, 208 in cycle 2 and 179 in cycle 3. Cycle 0 is the BLASTP curve. In cycles 1 to 3 the curves fall from 180 to about 120, drop steeply near accession 850, and nearly coincide. Panel B shows heatmaps of the 1,259 accessions that reach pE 60 in at least one cycle, in four groups: 820 at or above 60 in every cycle, 246 below 60 only in cycle 0, 24 at or above 60 only in cycles 1 and 2, and 169 at or above 60 only in cycle 1. The upper heatmap gives pE in each cycle, with E = 0 hits counted as pE 180, and the lower one the change from the previous cycle: nearly every accession rises from cycle 0 to cycle 1, and later cycles change little
/assets/img/bioinformatics-walkthrough/r: A precursor peptide made of a leader domain and a core. PTMs modify the core, and proteolysis then removes the leader domain, leaving the modified core
